findings.title: Partial null hardening leaves sibling caller unsafe
findings.snippet:
def list_fleet_devices_unsafe(rows):
    # Sibling endpoint still groups nullable keys → NPE / 500 risk remains.
    from collections import defaultdict

    out = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        device = map_device(row)
        out[device["org_id"]].append(device)  # crashes when device is None
    return out
findings.context: Diff hardens list_org_devices_safe by filtering null devices from map_device, but sibling caller list_fleet_devices_unsafe still indexes into the nullable device.
findings.what: Shared helper map_device can return None. One caller filters that null; the sibling caller still uses device["org_id"] without a null guard, so the NPE/500 path remains.
findings.why: N1 requires tracing every caller and sibling endpoint after a null fix. Approving only the hardened path leaves production crash risk on the unfixed sibling.
findings.fix_hint: Apply the same null filter before grouping in list_fleet_devices_unsafe (or harden map_device / a shared grouping helper used by both callers), and add a regression that covers both sibling callers with a null device row.

notes: null_safety_callers: traced. Callers of map_device: list_org_devices_safe (hardened), list_fleet_devices_unsafe (unsafe sibling). No mapped L2 stack skill installed for this Python fixture under strict profile.
